models_evaluated: UC Davis Health population health ML model (12-month hospitalization/ED visit risk)

links.outcome: Calibration and discrimination of risk model across race-ethnicity, gender, and HPI subgroups
links.effect: Significantly lower predicted hospitalization probabilities for African Americans (0.129, p=0.016), Hispanics (0.133, p=0.004), AAPI (0.120, p=0.018), multi-race (0.245, p=0.005) and low-HPI areas; ED AUROC below 0.8 for Hispanic (0.773) and Other (0.752); no gender difference.
links.quote: There was evidence of differential calibration by race-ethnicity for both ED visits and hospitalizations.

unlisted_practices: Applying a multi-step equity framework (BE-FAIR) with anti-racism lens, community engagement, and historical review to predictive model development
Using EHR smart phrase to inform patients a model identified them for outreach
Training outreach staff in cultural humility and varying outreach timing

models_evaluated: UC Davis Health 31-feature population health predictive model for 12-month hospitalization or emergency department visit risk

links.outcome: Model discrimination for emergency department visits across racial and ethnic groups
links.effect: ED-visit AUROC was 0.773 [0.747, 0.799] for Hispanic patients and 0.752 [0.696, 0.808] for Other race patients, versus 0.817 [0.804, 0.829] for White patients.
links.quote: The AUROC for ED visits was lowest and below 0.8 for the Hispanic and Other race group; AUROC was highest for AIAN although this may reflect the small sample size of this group.

links.effect: Predicted probabilities of hospitalization were significantly lower for African American, Hispanic, AAPI, multi-race, and low HPI patients.
links.quote: Calibration differed by race-ethnicity and HPI with significantly lower predicted probabilities of hospitalization for African Americans (0.129±0.051, p=0.016), Hispanics (0.133±0.047, p=0.004), AAPI (0.120±0.051, p=0.018), and multi-race (0.245±0.087, p=0.005) relative to white/Caucasians and for individuals in low HPI areas (0 - 25%, 0.178±0.042, p<0.001; 25 - 50%, 0.129±0.044, p=0.003).

links.effect: Patients in the unknown race category had 17% missing data.
links.quote: Patients within the unknown race category had 17% missing data and this population had clinical conditions that make it hard for patients to answer survey questions.

unlisted_practices: developing and applying an equity framework (BE-FAIR) to guide model development and implementation
